title: Model choices change the ESPRESSO prediction gain of HARPS-selected HD 20794 signals from -6.6 to 11.7 percent
abstract: We test whether a HARPS residual signal at 35 to 50 days predicts separate ESPRESSO observations of HD 20794. A central model selects 37.689 days and reduces ESPRESSO residual error by 9.05 percent. A conditional 30-day group interval is -17.62 to +24.08 percent. Across 27 nuisance models, selected periods range from 37.68 to 47.93 days and gains range from -6.59 to +11.75 percent. A fixed 40.114-day template increases error by 9.70 percent. A known 18.3142-day control reduces error by 28.95 percent. Simple HARPS activity and Earth-velocity controls retain the central weak gain. Selection, stellar noise, data processing and the approximate orbit model limit inference. No secure new planet or physical cause is found. Code, frozen nightly data, source hashes, sensitivity tables and offline steps are included. Job sci-1107-dell-astronomy-7dcc62a8f367; machine dell; model gpt-6.1-sol.

display.caption: A HARPS-only period scan and fixed-template ESPRESSO prediction gains. Positive gain means less residual error. The selected signal has a broad uncertainty interval.
Each point is one of 27 nuisance models. Each model selects its period using HARPS alone. Prediction gain changes sign across the tested models.
